questions.question: The Council of Ministers in a state is collectively responsible to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Legislature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The governance of Indian states follows the **Parliamentary system**, where the executive is drawn from and remains accountable to the legislature.
 
• According to **Article 164(2)** of the **Constitution of India**, the Council of Ministers shall be **collectively responsible** to the **Legislative Assembly** of the State.
 
• The term **collective responsibility** implies that the entire ministry is viewed as a single unit; they share joint responsibility for all decisions made by the **Cabinet**.
 
• If the **State Legislative Assembly** passes a **No-Confidence Motion** against the government, all ministers, including those belonging to the **Legislative Council** (in bicameral states), must resign collectively.
 
• This mechanism ensures that the **Council of Ministers** retains power only as long as it commands the majority support of the **elected representatives** of the people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Entities:**

 
 
• **Governor:** While the ministers are collectively responsible to the legislature, they hold office during the **pleasure of the Governor** under **Article 164(1)**, which represents their **individual responsibility**.
 
• **President:** The **President of India** is the constitutional head of the Union; state ministers do not have a direct line of responsibility to the President, though the Governor is appointed by the President.
 
• **Supreme Court:** The **Judiciary** acts as the guardian of the Constitution and can perform **Judicial Review** of executive actions, but the Council of Ministers is not politically responsible to the court.
 
• **State Legislature:** In many states, this includes both the **Legislative Assembly** (Vidhan Sabha) and the **Legislative Council** (Vidhan Parishad), though collective responsibility specifically targets the **Lower House**.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the joint sitting of Parliament provided?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 108**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 108** of the **Constitution of India** empowers the **President** to summon a **joint sitting** of both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha** to resolve a legislative deadlock.
 
• A deadlock occurs if a bill is rejected by the other House, if the Houses disagree on **amendments**, or if the second House remains silent for more than **six months**.
 
• The **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** presides over the joint sitting. In the Speaker's absence, the **Deputy Speaker** of the Lok Sabha or the **Deputy Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha takes the chair.
 
• The **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** (the Vice-President) does not preside over a joint sitting because they are not a member of either House of **Parliament**.
 
• Decisions in a joint sitting are taken by a **simple majority** of the total number of members of both Houses present and voting.
 
• This provision is applicable only to **Ordinary Bills** and **Financial Bills**, and it cannot be invoked for **Money Bills** or **Constitutional Amendment Bills**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 107**: Deals with the **introduction and passing of Bills**, specifying that except for Money and Financial Bills, a bill may originate in either House.
 
• **Article 109**: Details the **special procedure** for **Money Bills**, clarifying that they cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha and must be returned within **14 days**.
 
• **Article 110**: Provides the **definition of Money Bills**, which includes matters related to **taxation**, public expenditure, and the **Consolidated Fund of India**.
 
 
• The **Speaker's certificate** is required to endorse a bill as a Money Bill, and this decision is **final** and cannot be challenged in court or Parliament.

questions.question: What is the main medium of transmission in Indian folk and tribal music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oral tradition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oral tradition** is the fundamental medium for transmitting **Indian folk and tribal music**, where musical knowledge is inherited through **auditory learning** and **mimicry** rather than formal scripts or notation.
 
• This tradition relies on **collective memory**, allowing the **lyrics**, **melodies**, and **rhythms** to be passed down during **festivals**, **harvests**, and **lifecycle rituals** within communities like the **Bhils**, **Santhals**, and **Munda** tribes.
 
• It serves as a living archive for **regional dialects**, **indigenous folklore**, and **mythological narratives**, ensuring that the **cultural identity** of a group is preserved across centuries without the need for literacy.
 
• The flexibility of this medium allows for **spontaneous improvisation** and the evolution of styles, which is why folk forms like the **Baul** of Bengal or **Pandavani** of Chhattisgarh maintain a dynamic and organic character.
 
• In the absence of **written records**, the **oral medium** ensures that even the most complex **polyrhythmic structures** and **microtonal variations** are mastered by younger members through continuous **participation** in social gatherings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru-Shishya tradition**:

 
 
• This is a formal **pedagogical system** predominantly found in **Indian Classical Music** (both **Hindustani** and **Carnatic**).
 
• It involves a dedicated relationship where a disciple (shishya) lives with the teacher (guru) to master the intricacies of **Ragas**, **Talas**, and specific **Gharana** lineages.
 
 
 
• **Written notation**:
 
 
• While systems like the **Bhatkhande** and **Paluskar** notations were developed in the **20th century** to document classical compositions, they are rarely used in **tribal music**.
 
• The **unscripted nature** of folk music is what distinguishes it from **academic** or **Margi Sangeet**.
 
 
 
• **Audio recordings**:
 
 
• These are modern **technological tools** utilized by organizations like the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** and **ethnomusicologists** for **archival purposes**.
 
• While they help in the **preservation** of endangered art forms, they are not the **traditional primary medium** for the pedagogical transmission of folk music within indigenous communities.

questions.question: The rolling of thunder is mainly due to
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Successive reflections of sound**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Thunder is the sound produced by the **rapid expansion** and contraction of air surrounding a path of **lightning**, which heats the air to approximately **30,000 Kelvin**.
 
• The **rolling effect** or rumbling of thunder is primarily caused by the **successive reflections** of sound waves from various surfaces such as **clouds**, **mountains**, and different **layers of air** with varying densities.
 
• Since a lightning bolt can be several kilometers long, sound waves originate from different points along the bolt; these waves reach an observer at different times due to the distance variations and the **echoes** created by **multiple reflections**.
 
• The **acoustic energy** bounces between the **ground and clouds**, or between different cloud formations, preventing the sound from being a single sharp crack and turning it into a prolonged **rumble**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resonance of clouds**:

 
 
• Resonance involves a system vibrating at its **natural frequency**. Clouds are composed of water droplets and ice and do not possess the **structural rigidity** required to resonate and produce the rolling sound of thunder.
 
 
 
• **Interference of sound waves**:
 
 
• While **constructive and destructive interference** can occur when sound waves meet, it typically results in variations in **loudness** or intensity rather than the sustained, multi-second duration characteristic of a **thunder roll**.
 
 
 
• **Lightning effect**:
 
 
• Lightning is the **source** of the sound (the cause of the shockwave), but the term 'lightning effect' is too broad and does not specifically explain the **temporal prolongation** and reflection mechanism that creates the rolling sensation.
 
 
 
• **Speed of Sound vs. Light**:
 
 
• Light travels at approximately **3 x 10⁸ meters per second**, while sound travels at roughly **340 meters per second**. This discrepancy explains why **lightning** is seen almost instantly, while **thunder** is heard later.

questions.question: The Aravalli Range extends from which direction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Northeast to Southwest**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Aravalli Range** is one of the oldest **fold mountain systems** in the world, having its origins in the **Proterozoic Era**.
 
• The range extends for approximately **692 kilometers** (430 miles), stretching from **Delhi** in the northeast, passing through **Southern Haryana** and **Rajasthan**, and ending at **Palanpur** in **Gujarat** in the southwest.
 
• The orientation of the range is **Northeast to Southwest**, a position that makes it nearly parallel to the direction of the **Southwest Monsoon** winds, leading to lower rainfall in the **Thar Desert** region.
 
• It serves as a major **geographical divide**, separating the semi-arid **Marwar** region from the more fertile **Mewar** region in Rajasthan.
 
• The range acts as a barrier to the eastward expansion of the **Thar Desert**, protecting the fertile **Indo-Gangetic plains** from wind erosion and sand deposition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Shikhar**:

 
 
• Located in the **Mount Abu** hills, it is the highest peak of the **Aravalli Range** with an elevation of **1,722 meters**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrology and Rivers**:
 
 
• Several important rivers originate or are fed by the Aravallis, including the **Luni River** (which flows into the Rann of Kutch), the **Sabarmati**, and the **Banas River**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance**:
 
 
• The range is exceptionally rich in mineral resources, providing significant deposits of **copper**, **zinc**, **lead**, **silver**, and construction materials like **Makrana marble**.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Role**:
 
 
• It functions as a **wildlife corridor** and contains several protected areas, such as the **Sariska Tiger Reserve** and the **Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary**.

questions.question: The Rann of Kutch is located in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rann of Kutch** is a massive expanse of **seasonal salt marshes** located in the **Kutch District** of the Indian state of **Gujarat**.
 
• It is situated within the **Thar Desert** biogeographic province and is globally recognized as one of the largest **salt deserts** in the world.
 
• Geographically, the region is bifurcated into two distinct areas: the **Great Rann of Kutch**, which covers the northern part, and the **Little Rann of Kutch**, located to the southeast.
 
• The landscape is primarily composed of **saline mudflats** that remain underwater during the **monsoon** season and transform into a **White Desert** during the dry winter months due to salt crystallization.
 
• It shares an international boundary with the **Sindh** province of **Pakistan** to the north and is bordered by the **Gulf of Kutch** and the **Arabian Sea** to the south and west.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wildlife and Conservation**:

 
 
• The **Little Rann of Kutch** houses the **Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary**, which is the last remaining natural habitat for the **Indian Wild Ass** (Khur).
 
• The **Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary** is famous for **Flamingo City**, a massive breeding ground for **Greater Flamingos**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrology**:
 
 
• Several rivers like the **Luni**, **Banas**, and **Rupen** drain into the **Rann of Kutch**, making it an endorheic basin where water does not flow out to the ocean.
 
 
 
• **Culture and Economy**:
 
 
• The **Gujarat Tourism** department hosts the **Rann Utsav**, a three-month-long festival that showcases **Kutchi handicrafts**, traditional **Bhungas** (mud houses), and local **folk music**.
 
• The region is a significant hub for **salt production**, contributing a substantial percentage of **India** total salt output.

questions.question: The Serpent and the Rope (Novel) is written by ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Rao**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Serpent and the Rope** is a landmark semi-autobiographical novel written by **Raja Rao** and was first published in **1960**.
 
• The novel is deeply rooted in **Advaita Vedanta** philosophy and explores the quest for self-realization and the fundamental differences between **Eastern** and **Western** metaphysical perspectives.
 
• In **1964**, Raja Rao received the prestigious **Sahitya Akademi Award** for this work, which is considered one of the most profound philosophical novels in Indian English literature.
 
• The title refers to the classic **Vedantic metaphor** where an individual mistakes a rope for a serpent due to ignorance (**Maya**), symbolizing the nature of illusion and reality.
 
• The narrative follows **Ramaswamy**, a young Brahmin scholar in France, and his intellectual and spiritual struggle as his marriage to a French woman, **Madeleine**, begins to disintegrate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Rao** (1908−2006):

 
 
• One of the founding fathers of modern **Indian English fiction**.
 
• Awarded the **Neustadt International Prize for Literature** in **1988**.
 
• Famous for his debut novel **Kanthapura** (1938), which portrays the **Gandhian struggle** in a South Indian village.
 
 
 
• **R.K. Narayan**:
 
 
• Celebrated for creating the fictional town of **Malgudi**.
 
• Authored iconic works such as **The Guide**, **Swami and Friends**, and **The Financial Expert**.
 
 
 
• **Mulk Raj Anand**:
 
 
• Known for his realistic and empathetic depiction of the oppressed classes.
 
• Significant works include **Untouchable** (1935) and **Coolie** (1936).
 
 
 
• **Khushwant Singh**:
 
 
• Prominent journalist and novelist best known for **Train to Pakistan** (1956).
 
• Served as a member of the **Rajya Sabha** from 1980 to 1986.

questions.question: Which state elected the world's first democratically elected communist government, with EMS Namboodiripad as CM?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The state of **Kerala** made history in the **1957** assembly elections by electing the first non-Congress government in independent India.
 
• The **Communist Party of India (CPI)** emerged as the single largest party, winning **60 out of 126 seats** and securing the support of five independent members to form a majority.
 
• **Elamkulam Manakkal Sankaran Namboodiripad**, popularly known as **E.M.S. Namboodiripad**, was sworn in as the **Chief Minister** on **April 5, 1957**.
 
• This victory is widely recognized in political history as the first time a **Communist government** came to power through a **parliamentary democratic election** in a significant sub-national territory.
 
• The government initiated radical social changes, including the introduction of the **Kerala Agrarian Relations Bill** and the **Education Bill**, aimed at land redistribution and regulating private educational institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dismissal of the Government**:

 
 
• In **1959**, the central government led by the Indian National Congress invoked **Article 356** of the Indian Constitution for the first time to dismiss the **EMS Namboodiripad** ministry.
 
• This followed the **Vimochana Samaram** (Liberation Struggle), an intense protest movement led by various religious and community organizations against the state's reforms.
 
 
 
• **West Bengal**:
 
 
• The **Communist Party of India (Marxist)**, leading the **Left Front**, came to power in **West Bengal** much later, in **1977**, under the leadership of **Jyoti Basu**.
 
 
 
• **Tripura**:
 
 
• The **Left Front** established its first government in **Tripura** in **1978**, with **Nripen Chakraborty** serving as the first communist Chief Minister of the state.

questions.question: Healthy life expectancy in the Happiness Index is based on:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Expected years of healthy living**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Happiness Report** is a landmark survey that ranks global happiness based on six key variables: **GDP per capita**, **social support**, **healthy life expectancy**, **freedom to make life choices**, **generosity**, and **perceptions of corruption**.
 
• The metric for **Healthy Life Expectancy** specifically measures the average number of years a person is expected to live in **full health**, taking into account the years lived in less than full health due to disease or injury.
 
• The data used for this indicator is primarily extracted from the **World Health Organization (WHO)** **Global Health Observatory** database, which provides time-series data for over 190 countries.
 
• This indicator is distinct from standard life expectancy as it focuses on the **quality of physical well-being** rather than just the total duration of life, reflecting how long an individual can contribute to and enjoy society without significant disability.
 
• The **Happiness Index** is published annually by the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** to help guide public policy toward the well-being of citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Average years of schooling**:

 
 
• This is a critical component used in the **Human Development Index (HDI)** published by the **UNDP**.
 
• It measures the educational attainment of the population aged **25 years and older**.
 
 
 
• **Total fertility rate**:
 
 
• This is a **demographic indicator** representing the average number of children a woman would have during her reproductive years.
 
• It is used to analyze **population growth** and replacement levels rather than subjective or objective happiness levels.
 
 
 
• **Number of hospitals**:
 
 
• This serves as a measure of **healthcare infrastructure** and physical capacity.
 
• While it supports health outcomes, it is considered an input variable rather than a direct outcome of **population well-being** in the Happiness Index framework.

questions.question: What capability does Project NETRA provide to ISRO?

options.text: Space debris tracking and situational awareness

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Space debris tracking and situational awareness**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Project NETRA** (Network for space object Tracking and Analysis) is a dedicated initiative by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** aimed at establishing an early warning system in space.
 
• The primary function of the project is to provide **Space Situational Awareness (SSA)**, which involves monitoring, tracking, and predicting the movement of **space debris** and other orbital hazards.
 
• It helps in protecting India's functional satellites from potential collisions with **defunct satellites**, **rocket bodies**, and **fragmentation pieces** orbiting the Earth.
 
• By developing this indigenous capability, India significantly reduces its dependence on foreign agencies like the **U.S. Space Command** for information regarding orbital threats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infrastructure and Reach:**

 
 
• The network includes **high-power radars**, **optical telescopes**, and a centralized **control centre** located at **Bengaluru**.
 
• The project is designed to detect and track objects as small as **10 cm** at a range of up to **3,400 km**, covering **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)** and eventually expanding to **Geostationary Orbit (GEO)**.
 
 
 
• **Operational Utility:**
 
 
• The data collected is critical for performing **Collision Avoidance Manoeuvres (CAM)**, where a satellite's path is altered to avoid a predicted impact.
 
• It also monitors **space weather** and keeps track of **near-Earth objects (NEOs)** such as asteroids that could pose a threat to the planet.
 
• The project is an essential component of India's strategy to safeguard strategic assets like **INSAT** and **Remote Sensing** satellites.

questions.question: The Indian men's hockey team won its last Olympic gold medal in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1980**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian men's hockey team** secured its eighth and final **Olympic gold medal** at the **1980 Moscow Olympics**, ending a 16-year wait since their previous gold in 1964.
 
• The team was led by captain **Vasudevan Baskaran**, and the final was played at the **Minor Arena** of the **Central Lenin Stadium** in Moscow, Soviet Union.
 
• In a high-stakes final match, India defeated **Spain** with a score of **4-3** to clinch the top spot on the podium.
 
• **Surinder Singh Sodhi** was the standout performer and the leading goal-scorer for the Indian side during the tournament, contributing **15 goals** to the team's tally.
 
• This victory remains a landmark event as it was the last time the **Indian hockey team** stood on the highest pedestal at the **Summer Olympic Games**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legacy of Indian Olympic Hockey**:

 
 
• India's dominance in **Olympic field hockey** is unparalleled, with a total of **eight gold medals** won in **1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964**, and **1980**.
 
• The **Golden Era** (1928-1956) saw India winning **six consecutive gold medals**, a record that remains unbroken in the sport.
 
• Apart from the gold medals, India has also won **one silver medal (1960)** and **four bronze medals (1968, 1972, 2020, 2024)**.
 
 
 
• **Transition Challenges**:
 
 
• The introduction of **synthetic turf (Astroturf)** at the **1976 Montreal Olympics** significantly impacted India's performance, leading to a temporary decline in their global ranking as the team struggled to adapt from grass fields.
 
• Following the 1980 triumph, India entered a long **41-year medal drought** that was finally broken at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** under the captaincy of **Manpreet Singh**.

questions.question: India wants to explore Venus's thick atmosphere and greenhouse effect. Which mission is planned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shukrayaan (Venus Orbiter)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** is developing the **Venus Orbiter Mission (VOM)**, popularly referred to as **Shukrayaan**, to conduct a comprehensive study of the planet Venus.
 
• A primary objective of the mission is to explore the **stratospheric chemistry** and the **runaway greenhouse effect** that characterizes Venus's thick, toxic atmosphere, which is composed of over **96% Carbon Dioxide**.
 
• The mission aims to study **surface topography** and **subsurface layers** using **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)**, helping scientists understand the geological processes and potential volcanic activity on the planet.
 
• **Shukrayaan** will also investigate the **interaction of the solar wind** with the Venusian ionosphere and the planet's lack of a global intrinsic magnetic field.
 
• The spacecraft is expected to be launched using the **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark 3)**, placing it into a **highly elliptical orbit** to allow for varying altitudes during scientific observations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **LUPEX (Lunar Polar Exploration Mission)**:

 
 
• This is a joint mission between **ISRO** and the **Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA)**.
 
• It aims to send a **lunar rover and lander** to explore the **South Pole** region of the Moon specifically to investigate the quantity and quality of **water ice**.
 
 
 
• **Chandrayaan-4**:
 
 
• Following the success of **Chandrayaan-3**, this mission is conceptualized as a **Lunar Sample Return Mission**.
 
• Its core objective is to land on the lunar surface, collect **regolith samples**, and successfully return them to **Earth** for advanced laboratory analysis.
 
 
 
• **MOM-2 (Mars Orbiter Mission-2)**:
 
 
• Also known as **Mangalyaan-2**, it is the planned successor to India's first interplanetary mission.
 
• It will focus on more detailed **morphological, mineralogical, and atmospheric** studies of **Mars** using a more advanced suite of scientific instruments.

questions.question: The bank nationalization in 1969 was primarily aimed at:

options.text: Extending credit to agriculture, small industries, and priority sectors

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Extending credit to agriculture, small industries, and priority sectors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **July 19, 1969**, the Government of India, led by Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**, nationalized **14 major commercial banks** through the **Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance**.
 
• The primary objective was to ensure that credit was not concentrated in the hands of a few **industrial houses** and instead flowed to **neglected sectors** such as **agriculture**, **small-scale industries (SSIs)**, and **village artisans**.
 
• Nationalization marked a transition from **Class Banking** to **Mass Banking**, aiming to mobilize **domestic savings** and direct them toward **socially productive purposes** as outlined in the **Five-Year Plans**.
 
• Prior to 1969, private banks were heavily focused on **urban areas**; nationalization facilitated massive **branch expansion** into **unbanked rural** and semi-urban regions to reduce **regional disparities**.
 
• The move was intended to support the **Green Revolution** by providing institutional credit to farmers, thereby reducing their dependence on **local moneylenders** and high-interest debt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)**:

 
 
• Following nationalization, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** introduced **PSL norms**, mandating that a specific percentage of **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** must go to sectors like agriculture, **education**, **housing**, and **micro-enterprises**.
 
 
 
• **Second Phase of Nationalization**:
 
 
• In **April 1980**, another **6 commercial banks** were nationalized, bringing nearly **90%** of the banking business under **public sector** control.
 
 
 
• **Lead Bank Scheme**:
 
 
• Introduced in **1969** based on the **Nariman Committee** recommendations, it assigned specific districts to banks to act as **leaders** in coordinating credit deployment and **financial inclusion**.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options Context**:
 
 
• **Controlling inflation**: This is a function of **Monetary Policy** managed by the **RBI** through tools like **Repo Rate** and **CRR**, rather than bank ownership.
 
• **Promoting exports**: While exports became a **priority sector** later, the 1969 act was more focused on **domestic rural development** and credit democratization.

questions.question: Which economist gave the concept of comparative advantage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ricardo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **David Ricardo**, a prominent 19th-century British political economist, first formulated the **Theory of Comparative Advantage** in his seminal work, **On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation**, published in **1817**.
 
• The concept explains that international trade can be mutually beneficial even if one nation has an **absolute advantage** in producing every single good; the key lies in **relative efficiency** and **opportunity cost**.
 
• **Opportunity cost** refers to the value of the next best alternative foregone; **Ricardo** argued that countries should specialize in producing goods where their **opportunity cost** is the lowest compared to other nations.
 
• He famously illustrated this using the example of **England and Portugal** producing **cloth and wine**, demonstrating that total global output increases when each nation focuses on its **comparative strength**.
 
• This theory remains a cornerstone of **classical international trade theory** and provides the fundamental logical justification for **free trade** policies globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adam Smith**:

 
 
• Known as the **Father of Modern Economics**, he authored **The Wealth of Nations** in **1776**.
 
• He introduced the **Theory of Absolute Advantage**, suggesting that a country should specialize in goods it can produce more efficiently than any other.
 
 
 
• **John Maynard Keynes**:
 
 
• A 20th-century economist who founded **Keynesian Economics** and wrote **The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money** (1936).
 
• His work focused on **macroeconomic management**, **aggregate demand**, and the role of **government intervention** during economic recessions.
 
 
 
• **John Hicks**:
 
 
• An influential British economist known for his contributions to **general equilibrium theory** and **welfare economics**.
 
• He developed the **IS-LM model**, which serves as a graphical representation of **Keynesian macroeconomic theory**.

questions.question: Which of the following most accurately reflects the fundamental orientation of public sector industries in India?

options.text: They function with the exclusive motive of profit maximization
They are predominantly under foreign ownership and control
They prioritize wider socio-economic developmental objectives

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**prioritize wider socio-economic developmental objectives**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) in India were established with the primary vision of achieving a **socialistic pattern of society**, as envisioned in the early Five-Year Plans.
 
• The fundamental orientation of these industries is to ensure **balanced regional development** by setting up units in backward or underdeveloped areas to stimulate local economies.
 
• Under the **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956**, the public sector was given the 'commanding heights' of the economy to build a strong **industrial infrastructure** (like steel and power) that the private sector was unable or unwilling to fund at the time.
 
• These enterprises focus on **employment generation** and providing essential goods and services at **subsidized or controlled prices** to ensure they remain accessible to the common masses.
 
• They serve as a tool for the **redistribution of income and wealth**, preventing the concentration of economic power in the hands of a few private individuals or corporations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Profit Maximization vs. Social Welfare**:

 
 
• While private sectors operate purely for **shareholder profit**, PSUs prioritize **public interest**. However, through reforms, the government now encourages **financial viability** and efficiency in these units.
 
 
 
• **Ownership and Control**:
 
 
• Public sector industries are defined by having at least **51 percent** of the paid-up share capital held by the **Central Government**, **State Government**, or both. They are not under foreign control.
 
 
 
• **Classification of PSUs**:
 
 
• To improve competitiveness, the government grants specific statuses such as **Maharatna**, **Navratna**, and **Miniratna** based on their financial performance and global presence.
 
• **Maharatna** companies (like **NTPC** or **ONGC**) have the highest level of **operational autonomy** to make large-scale investments without prior government approval.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance**:
 
 
• Enterprises in the public sector often manage **strategic sectors** like atomic energy, defense equipment, and railway transport to maintain **national security** and sovereignty.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the East India Company ultimately annexed Punjab?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1849**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formal annexation of **Punjab** by the **British East India Company** took place on **March 29, 1849**, marking the end of the **Sikh Empire** founded by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.
 
• The annexation was the direct result of the **Second Anglo-Sikh War** (1848−1849), which concluded after the decisive British victory at the **Battle of Gujrat** in February **1849**.
 
• **Lord Dalhousie**, the **Governor-General of India** from 1848 to 1856, issued the proclamation of annexation, citing the need to maintain stability on the northwestern frontier.
 
• The last Sikh ruler, **Maharaja Duleep Singh**, who was a minor at the time, was forced to sign the **Treaty of Lahore**, surrendering all claims to the sovereignty of the region and the **Koh-i-Noor diamond**.
 
• Following the annexation, **Punjab** was governed by a **Board of Administration** composed of **Henry Lawrence**, **John Lawrence**, and **Charles Mansel**, which focused on land reforms and infrastructure development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Historical Context of Other Options:
 
 
• **1836**: During this period, **Maharaja Ranjit Singh** was still in power and maintained a strong diplomatic relationship with the British through the **Treaty of Amritsar** (1809).
 
• **1841**: This year was characterized by extreme internal political instability and successive assassinations within the **Lahore Darbar** following the death of Ranjit Singh in 1839.
 
• **1856**: This year is notable for the annexation of **Awadh** (Oudh) by **Lord Dalhousie** under the pretext of alleged misgovernment, which was a significant catalyst for the **Revolt of 1857**.
 
• The **First Anglo-Sikh War** (1845−1846) preceded the annexation and resulted in the **Treaty of Lahore**, where the British established a residency and annexed the **Jalandhar Doab**.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: In which of the following year the Court of Directors of the East India Company in London sent an educational (Wood's) dispatch to the Governor-General in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1854**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Wood's Despatch** was an educational dispatch sent in **1854** by the **Court of Directors** of the **East India Company** to the **Governor-General** of India.
 
• It was prepared by **Sir Charles Wood**, who served as the **President of the Board of Control**, and is famously known as the **'Magna Carta of English Education in India'**.
 
• The primary objective of the dispatch was to create a properly articulated scheme of education from the primary school level up to the **University level**.
 
• It emphasized that the **Government of India** must take responsibility for the education of the masses, moving away from the earlier **'Downward Filtration Theory'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Recommendations and Impact**:

 
 
• It recommended the establishment of **Departments of Public Instruction** in provinces like **Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Punjab,** and the **North-Western Provinces**.
 
• The dispatch paved the way for the establishment of universities in **Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras** in **1857**, modeled after the **University of London**.
 
• It advocated for **English** as the medium of instruction for higher studies, while **Vernacular languages** were encouraged at the school level to ensure wider reach.
 
• The policy stressed the importance of **Female education** and **Vocational training**, recognizing the need for practical and technical skills among the Indian population.
 
• It introduced a system of **Grants-in-aid** to encourage private enterprise in the field of education, provided the schools maintained certain secular and academic standards.
